content: {"mechanism":{"summary":"The gateway builds a key from the API key and route group, then runs one atomic script in a shared store: read the token count and last refill time, add the tokens earned since then (elapsed seconds times refill rate, capped at capacity), spend one token if any remain, and write the new state back. If no token is left it answers 429 with a Retry-After header computed from the refill rate. The atomicity is the point: without it two gateway nodes read the same count, both see a token, and both admit a request.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-1","source-1#chunk-2"],"steps":[{"text":"Build the limiter key from the API key and the route group, for example key:7781:search.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-1"]},{"text":"Read two fields for that key from the shared store: the token count and the timestamp of the last refill.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-1"]},{"text":"Add the tokens earned since that timestamp (elapsed seconds times the refill rate), capped at the bucket's capacity.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-1"]},{"text":"If at least one token is left, take one, write the new count and timestamp back, and let the request through.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-1"]},{"text":"Otherwise answer 429 Too Many Requests and compute Retry-After from the refill rate.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-1"]},{"text":"Run read, refill and write as one atomic script inside the store, so two gateway nodes cannot both spend the same last token.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-2"]},{"text":"When a store call is slower than the timeout or errors, apply the configured policy: fail closed with an error, or fall back to per-instance limits.","sourceChunkIds":["source-2#chunk-2","source-3#chunk-1"]}]},"plainSummary":"A rate limiter decides, per request, whether this caller may go now. Each caller has a bucket of tokens; one token is permission for one request. Tokens refill at a fixed rate, so an idle caller can save up a burst. The bucket lives in one shared store, so every front-end server sees the same count. If that store is slow, the choice is refuse requests or risk over-sending.","analogies":[{"analogy":"A bucket of coins by a door: each entry costs one coin, and a machine drops in a new coin at a steady drip, stopping when the bucket is full.","matches":"The bucket's rim is the capacity, the drip is the refill rate, and each entry is a request that spends a token; a quiet period fills the bucket so several people can enter at once.","breaksDown":"Nothing physically waits for the drip: the limiter does not refill on a timer, it computes how many tokens would have arrived from the elapsed time, capped at capacity."},{"analogy":"One shared notebook at a club's front desk, so every doorman checks the same page before letting someone in.","matches":"The notebook is the shared store: all gateway nodes read and write the same per-key state instead of each keeping a private count.","breaksDown":"A human can read the page, get interrupted, and write later; the real system needs that check-and-update to be one indivisible step, or two doormen let the same last entry through."}],"glossary":[{"term":"token bucket","plainMeaning":"A bucket of permission tokens that refills at a fixed rate; each request spends one token.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-1"]},{"term":"capacity","plainMeaning":"The most tokens a bucket can hold, which sets the biggest burst a caller can make.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-1"]},{"term":"refill rate","plainMeaning":"How many tokens come back per second, which sets the steady request rate.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-1"]},{"term":"Retry-After","plainMeaning":"A response header saying how many seconds until the next token arrives.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-1"]},{"term":"limiter key","plainMeaning":"The identifier a limit is counted against, here built from API key plus route group.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-1"]},{"term":"atomic script","plainMeaning":"A read-refill-write that the store runs as one indivisible step, so no other node interleaves.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-2"]},{"term":"shared store","plainMeaning":"One in-memory service holding all the buckets, so every instance sees the same count.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-2","source-2#chunk-1"]},{"term":"fixed window","plainMeaning":"Counting requests per calendar minute and resetting the counter at the minute boundary.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-2"]},{"term":"sliding window log","plainMeaning":"Storing the timestamp of every request in the window and counting them; exact but memory-heavy.","sourceChunkIds":["source-2#chunk-1"]},{"term":"sliding window counter","plainMeaning":"Keeping only this window's and the previous window's counts, weighting the old one; cheap but approximate.","sourceChunkIds":["source-2#chunk-1"]},{"term":"fail closed","plainMeaning":"Refusing requests when the limiter's store is unreachable, instead of serving traffic it cannot count.","sourceChunkIds":["source-2#chunk-2","source-3#chunk-2"]},{"term":"local fallback","plainMeaning":"Each instance enforces the limit alone while the store is down, multiplying the effective limit by the instance count.","sourceChunkIds":["source-2#chunk-2"]}],"facts":[{"id":"fact-1","statement":"A token bucket keeps two values per key: a token count capped at the bucket's capacity, and the timestamp of the last refill; each request takes one token.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-1"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"fact-2","statement":"At the invented Hollowmere gateway, a free-tier key gets a capacity of 100 tokens and a refill rate of 10 tokens per second, so a quiet client can burst 100 requests and then settles to 10 requests per second.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-1"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"fact-3","statement":"When the bucket is empty the request is refused with HTTP 429 Too Many Requests and a Retry-After header giving the seconds until the next token.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-1"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"fact-4","statement":"The limiter key is built from the API key and the route group, for example key:7781:search, so limits are per caller per route group.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-1"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"fact-5","statement":"Refill is computed, not scheduled: tokens added equal elapsed seconds times the refill rate, capped at capacity.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-1"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"fact-6","statement":"The read, refill and write must run as one atomic script inside the store; otherwise two gateway nodes can read the same count, both see one token left, and both let a request through.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-2"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"fact-7","statement":"Hollowmere runs 24 gateway nodes behind a load balancer; per-node buckets would give a client spread across all of them 24 times its limit.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-2"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"fact-8","statement":"A shared store costs a network round trip on every request: 0.4 ms median and 2.1 ms at p99 in measurements from June 2024.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-2"],"confidence":"medium"},{"id":"fact-9","statement":"The first version counted requests per calendar minute and reset the counter at the top of each minute: cheap, one counter per key, but a client could spend its whole quota in the last second of one minute and again in the first second of the next, up to 2 times the limit inside two seconds.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-2"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"fact-10","statement":"The token bucket was chosen over the fixed window because capacity bounds bursts no matter where the clock is.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-2"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"fact-11","statement":"A rate limiter protects fairness between well-behaved clients, not the service from a flood: a real flood of 2 million requests per second still reaches the gateways, which must parse each request and look up its key before refusing it; dropping that traffic is the network edge's job.","sourceChunkIds":["source-1#chunk-2"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"fact-12","statement":"The sliding window log stores one timestamp per request and is exact, but memory grows with the limit: at 8 bytes per timestamp, a limit of 1,000 requests per minute costs about 8 KB per active key, and 500,000 active keys come to around 4 GB.","sourceChunkIds":["source-2#chunk-1"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"fact-13","statement":"The sliding window counter keeps only the current and previous window's counts and weights the previous one by how much of it still overlaps; it needs 2 counters per key and is approximate because it assumes the previous window's requests were evenly spread.","sourceChunkIds":["source-2#chunk-1"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"fact-14","statement":"quotaflow's store timeout defaults to 50 ms; a slower store call counts as a store failure.","sourceChunkIds":["source-2#chunk-2"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"fact-15","statement":"quotaflow's default on store failure is fail closed: it refuses the request with 503 rather than serving traffic it cannot count.","sourceChunkIds":["source-2#chunk-2"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"fact-16","statement":"quotaflow's local fallback is off by default; when enabled, each instance enforces the limit alone while the store is down, which multiplies the effective limit by the number of instances.","sourceChunkIds":["source-2#chunk-2"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"fact-17","statement":"Clock skew between instances does not affect quotaflow because timestamps are taken inside the store.","sourceChunkIds":["source-2#chunk-2"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"fact-18","statement":"Keys are not expired until 2 windows after their last request, so memory for idle keys lingers briefly.","sourceChunkIds":["source-2#chunk-2"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"fact-19","statement":"At Larkspur Pay, 31% of checkout requests failed for 47 minutes on 14 March 2025 after the rate limiter's shared store became slow and the limiter fell back to local limits on each instance.","sourceChunkIds":["source-3#chunk-1"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"fact-20","statement":"A routine failover moved the limiter's store to a replica in another zone; store calls went from about 1 ms to 80 ms.","sourceChunkIds":["source-3#chunk-1"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"fact-21","statement":"Calls over the 50 ms store timeout counted as failures and the limiter was configured to fail open, so each Larkspur's traffic.","sourceChunkIds":["source-3#chunk-1"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"fact-22","statement":"Larkspur chose fail open for checkout deliberately, reasoning that refusing payments contract.","sourceChunkIds":["source-3#chunk-2"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"fact-23","statement":"After the incident Larkspur made the payment-provider limiter fail closed, divided local fallback limits by the number of instances, and raised the checkout limiter's store timeout from 50 ms to 150 ms, above a cross-zone round
